CSESS16.reason: Offers AUTH_NONE, AUTH_SYS, and an RPCSEC_GSS callback handle the server never issued, and expects NFS4_OK. The server answers NFS4ERR_NOENT, which RFC 8881 states CREATE_SESSION will return and BACKCHANNEL_CTL MUST return for an unknown handle. A server may instead read csa_sec_parms as a list to choose from and ignore the unusable entry; see #167.
CSESS16.reference: RFC 8881 Sections 18.33.3 (MUST, BACKCHANNEL_CTL) and 18.36.3 (will return, CREATE_SESSION)

CSESS29.reason: After 10,000 CREATE_SESSION requests that fail with NFS4ERR_TOOSMALL, sends new channel attributes with the same csa_sequenceid and expects NFS4_OK. Phase 2 moves the slot to the expected csa_sequenceid before session creation fails, so the reuse is a replay of the cached NFS4ERR_TOOSMALL. Reusing a sequence ID for a new request is also the client's error, since a retry MUST use the same csa_sequence. Section 18.36.4 presents these phases as a possible implementation.
CSESS29.reference: RFC 8881 Section 18.36.4, phase 2 and the csa_sequence retry MUST
